name: Threshold-activated discount
description:
This design adds a third discount to Sales pricing: a percentage off a single product's price that applies only when the price strictly exceeds a threshold ([Discount above a threshold](noesis:need|threshold-discount)).

# Where it lands

- The [Discounts](noesis:module|Sales.Pricing.Discounts) module of Sales pricing, beside the two existing discounts (spec, A1). Nothing else in Sales changes.

# Where to start reading

1. [Discount](noesis:building_block|Sales.Pricing.Discounts.Discount) is the one type callers hold. It gains a third variant, made by the new [Discount.Threshold](noesis:behavior|Sales.Pricing.Discounts.Discount.Threshold), while [Discount.Percentage](noesis:behavior|Sales.Pricing.Discounts.Discount.Percentage) and [Discount.Value](noesis:behavior|Sales.Pricing.Discounts.Discount.Value) keep their signatures (spec, A3; [One discount for callers](noesis:need|one-discount-for-callers)). [Discount.ApplyOn](noesis:behavior|Sales.Pricing.Discounts.Discount.ApplyOn) dispatches across all three.
2. [ThresholdDiscount](noesis:building_block|Sales.Pricing.Discounts.ThresholdDiscount) is the new value object: a percentage and a strictly positive threshold, rejected when it is made with invalid input (spec, A4; [No malformed discount](noesis:need|no-malformed-discount)).
3. [ThresholdDiscount.ApplyOn](noesis:behavior|Sales.Pricing.Discounts.ThresholdDiscount.ApplyOn) reduces the price by the percentage only when the price is above the threshold; at the threshold or below it, the price is unchanged (spec, A2).

# Around them

- [PercentageDiscount](noesis:building_block|Sales.Pricing.Discounts.PercentageDiscount) and [ValueDiscount](noesis:building_block|Sales.Pricing.Discounts.ValueDiscount) are in the design only so this green-field model shows the whole module; they do not change ([Existing discounts unchanged](noesis:need|existing-discounts-unchanged)).

# Left for later

- Persisting the third variant (spec, A5).
- Cart-level thresholds, time-bounded promotions and new stacking rules (spec, A6).

added.id: rule|Sales.Pricing.Discounts.ThresholdDiscountIsOnlyConstructibleWhenInputsAreValid

description.value: Trigger: `ThresholdDiscount.Of(Percentage value, Money threshold)` is invoked. Pre-conditions: `value` and `threshold` are present. Algorithm: 1. The `Percentage` value object guarantees `value` lies within `[0%, 100%]` — no additional check is performed here (delegate, do not duplicate). 2. Inspect `threshold`: if it is non-positive (≤ zero in its currency), reject construction with a clear domain error indicating the threshold must be strictly positive. 3. If both checks pass, build the immutable instance via the private constructor and return it. Post-conditions: every existing instance has a percentage in `[0%, 100%]` and a strictly positive threshold; apply-time code can rely on this without re-checking. Edge cases: a zero threshold is rejected; a negative threshold is rejected; the rejection happens at the factory boundary so no invalid instance ever escapes.
description.author: agent

added.id: rule|Sales.Pricing.Discounts.DiscountActivatesOnlyAboveThreshold

description.value: Trigger: `ApplyOn(price)` is called on a constructed `ThresholdDiscount`. Pre-conditions: the instance is valid by construction (percentage in range, threshold strictly positive). Algorithm: 1. Evaluate the predicate `price > threshold` using strict greater-than. 2. If true, compute and return `price * (Percentage.Of100 - value)` — same reduction formula as `PercentageDiscount.ApplyOn`. 3. If false, return `price` unchanged. Post-conditions: when the predicate is true, the result is the price reduced by the configured percentage; when false, the result equals the input price. Edge cases: `price == threshold` returns the price unchanged — the comparison is strict, matching the worked example (500 PLN at a 500-PLN threshold yields 500 PLN). A `0`-PLN threshold is not constructible (rejected by the factory), so the activation predicate cannot be trivially satisfied by a zero-threshold instance.
description.author: agent

added.id: rule|Sales.Pricing.Discounts.DiscountUnionDispatchIsExhaustiveAcrossThreeVariants

description.value: Trigger: any operation on a `Discount` value that dispatches by variant — `ApplyOn(Money)`, `Equals`, `GetHashCode`, `ToString`. Pre-conditions: the `Discount` is valid by construction (built through one of the three public static factories `Discount.Percentage`, `Discount.Value`, `Discount.Threshold`). Algorithm: 1. The discriminator field is a three-valued enum-like state — every dispatch must cover all three branches. 2. For each operation, route to the corresponding underlying value object: percentage variant → `_percentageDiscount`; value variant → `_valueDiscount`; threshold variant → `_thresholdDiscount`. 3. The non-active variant fields are at their default values and must not be observed. Post-conditions: every dispatch yields a single deterministic answer; no fallthrough or default branch is ever taken because the discriminator's three states cover every constructible `Discount`. Edge cases: introducing a fourth variant in the future would require updating every dispatch site — the rule mandates that an exhaustive switch (or equivalent) is used, not an `if/else` cascade that silently ignores an unknown discriminator value.
description.author: agent

added.id: rule|Sales.Pricing.Discounts.ExistingDiscountFactorySignaturesAreStable

description.value: Trigger: any change to the `Discount` type that touches its factory surface. Pre-conditions: the existing public static factories `Discount.Percentage(Percentage value)` and `Discount.Value(Money value)` exist and have known signatures relied upon by call sites across the solution. Algorithm: 1. The two existing factory methods MUST keep their exact current signatures and observable behavior. 2. New variants are added via additional public static factories (here: `Discount.Threshold(Percentage value, Money threshold)`); they do not replace, rename, or alter the existing two. 3. The internal discriminator implementation is allowed to change (e.g. bool → enum-like) provided this stability rule for the public factories is preserved. Post-conditions: existing call sites compile and behave identically; the only API surface change visible to callers is the new factory. Edge cases: any rename or signature change of the existing factories is treated as a breaking change and is out of scope of this design doc.

name.value: A Discount always holds exactly one valid discount
name.author: agent

description.value: A `Discount` is made only by one of its factories, and only from a discount that could itself be made: when the underlying discount is rejected, the rejection reaches the caller and no `Discount` exists, never a partly made one. The kinds of discount it does not hold are never observed.
